definition: Abrogate means to abolish or cancel, usually by official authority.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abrogate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abrogate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: With one signature, the queen abrogated the nobles' ancient hunting privileges in the royal forest.
To waive a rule is far milder than to abrogate it: the rule is set aside for one case and lives on for every other.
Repeal stops a step short of abrogate: it removes one statute by the usual process, while abrogate sweeps a whole law or treaty aside by naked authority.

To rescind is to take back a single order, offer, or decision — the authority that issued it withdraws it. Abrogate reaches further: it kills an entire law, treaty, or standing arrangement, not one decision. Rescind undoes one ruling; abrogate erases the whole framework around it.

Scrap is the informal, everyday word for junking a plan or rule — a coach scraps a play, a family scraps a trip. Abrogate is official power doing the same job formally, killing a law or treaty by authority. You scrap your own plans; governments abrogate binding arrangements.

For forty years, a compact between the two states set every rule of the shared river: who drew water, who dredged, who paid.
Then the new governor, impatient with its limits, pressed the legislature to abrogate the agreement outright.
Critics begged for half-measures -- suspend a clause here, renegotiate a fee there -- but the bill erased the whole framework at a stroke.
The morning it passed, decades of schedules, quotas, and joint patrols simply ceased to exist.
Neighboring farmers, who had planned their seasons around the compact, woke to find that no rule of the river remained in force.
